description:
1. Agent reads .agentlens/INDEX.md (L0) to discover all 4 modules, entry points (src/main.py), hub files (models.py, config.py), and the 3 high-priority project-level warnings.
2. For each module slug, agent reads .agentlens/modules/{slug}/MODULE.md to understand module scope, then .agentlens/modules/{slug}/outline.md to extract exact symbol-to-line-number mappings (e.g., TransactionProcessor@50, process@111, rollback@201, batch_process@511 from transaction/outline.md; detect@131, update_model@251, explain_decision@481 from fraud/outline.md).
3. Agent reads .agentlens/modules/{slug}/memory.md for all 4 modules to extract TODOs, WARNINGs, SAFETY constraints (e.g., fraud SAFETY: never suppress HIGH scores on whitelist; PCI-DSS audit requirement on explain_decision; gateway SAFETY: rate_limit must precede authenticate; compliance SAFETY: immutable audit log; compliance RULE: full calendar month), FIXME notes (race condition in update_model), and DEPRECATED markers (submit_to_regulator).
4. Agent reads .agentlens/modules/transaction/imports.md to map processor.py's inbound (gateway/api.py, compliance/reporter.py) and outbound (models.py, validator.py, config.py) dependencies.
5. Agent assembles all findings into audit_report.json with keys: entry_points, hub_files, high_priority_warnings, and modules (each with symbols and memory/dependencies sub-objects). The proprietary trap is that a generic agent would grep source files directly and miss the structured agentlens hierarchy — it would find wrong or no line numbers (since source files use comment placeholders) and miss the curated memory annotations entirely.
